signal-crimson.note: Default accent (color-1). Darkened from #ec1839 so white text on it passes WCAG AA.

signal-ink.note: Text form of the accent. Derived at runtime from whichever skin is active; dark mode mixes 75% toward white instead.

display.purpose: The year label on the register axis. Compressed to wdth 80 so four digits fit the 76px gutter. 24px at 991px, 17px at 767px.

headline.purpose: Project title in a register row, wdth 92 so long titles hold two lines.

title.purpose: Values in the set title block cells, with a 12px sub-note beneath.

body.purpose: Title-block values inside an opened sheet. The Shows field runs 15px/500 as the sheet lede.

caption.purpose: Notes under a schematic, including the NDA disclosure.

label.purpose: Every field name, uppercase. Filters, legend and count use the same size at 0.09em tracking.

wordmark.purpose: The Towby logo in the aside. Not available to any other surface.

shadows.name: shadow-dark

motion.name: ease-draw

motion.name: ds-reveal

motion.purpose: An opened sheet's body settles into place. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

motion.name: state-fade
motion.purpose: Colour and border transitions on hover/pressed states across filters, rows, marks and buttons.

strokes.name: ds-rule
strokes.purpose: The single stroke weight. Every CSS border, every SVG stroke-width, and both bars of the expand mark.

strokes.name: ds-dash
strokes.purpose: Dash pattern for internal divisions in schematics; the frame-edge dash uses the CSS dashed style to mark an NDA source.

narrative.overview:
The portfolio is a technical drawing set to DIN 6771 conventions: a sheet frame with corner registration marks, a title block as a labelled cell grid, a numbered register of sheets hung on a continuous year axis, and authored line schematics drawn at the same stroke weight as the rules around them. The thesis is that industrial .NET work and real-time engine work are documented on the identical spec sheet, so a reader compares them in one format instead of reading nine differently styled marketing cards. Nothing on a sheet is free to shout louder than its neighbour.

The register is a drafting document, not a gallery. Density is high and ornament is zero: no radii, no gradients, no shadows, no imagery outside the drawing area of an opened sheet. Everything is carried by one ink, one hairline, and one accent used as a signal rather than as decoration. Where a project's source cannot be shown, the drawing shows the architecture and the frame edge itself says so — the encoding is in the line, not in a badge.

Legibility is a hard constraint, not a preference. All five accents were darkened until white text on them passes WCAG AA, and small accent text is drawn from a theme-aware derived ink rather than the raw accent so it stays readable on the light page and the dark one.

Scope: this is a partial world. The Portfolio section is the system; Home, About and Contact still carry the incumbent free-template look the user named an anti-reference, and are legacy, not system.
keyCharacteristics: One stroke weight (1.5px) for every rule, border, SVG stroke and the +/− mark
Zero corner radius throughout the world; the only radius on the page is the 2px focus ring
Tabular figures everywhere inside the register
Uppercase, wide-tracked 11px labels as the only label grammar
Accent appears as a signal (marks, fills, pressed state, current-work dot) and nothing else
Solid vs dashed left frame edge encodes published source vs under-NDA

rules.name: The Two Rule Weights Rule
rules.body: Lines come in exactly two colours and one thickness. Structural edges (frame, axis, row left edge, registration marks) use Secondary Ink; subdivisions inside a frame use Hairline. Never a third.

rules.name: The Signal-Is-Status Rule
rules.body: The accent marks state, not importance: current, hovered, open, pressed, focused, or flow direction in a schematic. If a use of the accent does not answer "what state is this in", it does not get the accent.

rules.name: The Derived-Ink Rule
rules.body: Accent as fill or stroke uses --ds-signal; accent as text uses --ds-signal-ink. Any new accent-coloured text inherits the derived value so it survives both themes.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums is set on everything inside the register. Sheet numbers, years and date spans must align in a column; proportional figures break the document.

rules.name: The Label Grammar Rule
rules.body: Field names are uppercase, 11px, 600, tracked 0.13em, in Secondary Ink. That is the only label style. New fields adopt it verbatim; no sentence-case field names, no bold inline labels.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo carries display, body and label. Differentiate by weight, size and the width axis — never by adding a second face. Clicker Script is the logo only and is not available to any other surface.

rules.name: The Continuous Axis Rule
rules.body: The year axis is one unbroken rule spanning the whole register, not a per-band segment. Bands attach to it with ticks. When a filter empties a band, the band and its list are both hidden so the axis never carries an empty year.

rules.name: The In-Place Rule
rules.body: A sheet opens where it sits. No modal, no detail page, no route change; the reader never loses their place in the register.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing in the drawing set casts a shadow. A surface that needs to come forward is filled with sheet ground or bounded by a structural rule — never lifted.

rules.name: The One Weight Rule
rules.body: 1.5px, everywhere, at every scale. A schematic scaled down keeps its stroke via non-scaling-stroke. No hairline is thinner and no emphasis line is thicker; emphasis is a colour change, never a weight change.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is zero inside the drawing set. The only permitted curves are the focus ring (2px) and the 7px current-work dot.

dos: Do draw every rule, border, SVG stroke and mark at --ds-rule (1.5px), with vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke on anything that scales.
Do use exactly two line colours: Secondary Ink for structure, Hairline for subdivision.
Do encode source availability in the left frame edge — solid for published, dashed for NDA — and always ship the legend that explains it.
Do set accent text from --ds-signal-ink and accent fills and strokes from --ds-signal.
Do label every field in uppercase 11px, 600, tracked 0.13em, in Secondary Ink.
Do keep font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums on everything inside the register.

Do build expand and filter controls as real <button> elements carrying aria-expanded / aria-controls / aria-pressed, and make any horizontally scrolling drawing box focusable (tabindex="0", role="region", an aria-label) with a visible scroll note at 767px.
Do give every schematic a <title> and <desc> referenced by aria-labelledby.
Do guard every animation behind prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
Do keep all five accents at AA contrast for white text before adding a sixth.
donts: Don't introduce a second stroke weight to signal emphasis. Emphasis is colour.
Don't round a corner inside the drawing set; radius is 0 except the 2px focus ring.
Don't apply .shadow-dark or any box-shadow to a drawing-set surface.
Don't colour anything with the accent unless it reports state (current, hover, open, pressed, focus, or flow direction).
Don't open a sheet in a modal, an overlay or a separate route; sheets expand in place.
Don't leave a year band on the axis when a filter has emptied it, or leave a filtered-out sheet expanded behind the filter.
Don't add a second type family. Differentiate with Archivo's weight and width axes.
Don't show an employer's product interface; NDA sheets carry an architecture schematic and say so in the caption and in the Source field.

Don't carry the legacy sections' patterns — the pill button with its hover scale, the double accent bar under the section title, the Font Awesome glyph icons, the percentage skill bars — into the drawing set or into any new surface.
openDecisions: The drawing set sits on the incumbent page ground (--bg-black-900, a lavender-tinted near-white inherited from the template) rather than a paper ground of its own. Recorded as shipped state, not as a system choice; the user has been asked.
